problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix $A$ above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3.$ Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{T}\,AP.$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. 
Given that $D={P}^{T}\,AP,$ where $P$ is an orthogonal matrix, which of the following could be the second column of the matrix $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if there exists an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that

$$
A=PD{P}^{T},
$$

where $D$ is a diagonal matrix. Equivalently,

$$
D={P}^{T}AP.
$$

Moreover, a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if and only if it is symmetric.

First, note that $A$ is symmetric and $D$ is diagonal. Therefore, $D={P}^{T}\,AP$ gives an orthogonal diagonalization of $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ 

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ Computing $A-1I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{2}.$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm, we obtain the second column of $P:$ 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$
